{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011Cg7gATBWuQ3yuqHeHUZvW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The nbody benchmark now runs as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program, and its output is bit-identical to the original serial code in every test.\n\n**What changed** (only `nbody/nbody.cpp` and `nbody/CMakeLists.txt`, executable still named `nbody`):\n\n- **MPI** partitions the bodies into contiguous slices, one per rank. Each rank owns its slice's velocities and keeps a replicated copy of all positions, refreshed each step with an in-place `MPI_Allgatherv`. Ranks map to GPUs by node-local rank, so multiple ranks per node spread across the node's GPUs.\n- **CUDA** does the all-pairs force kernel (shared-memory tiled, one thread per local body) and the integration on the device. Only the local position slice is downloaded per step. The block size adapts to the local problem size so small runs still fill the GPU.\n- **OpenMP** parallelizes the host-side work: array packing, finite/bounds validation, and the energy computation, which is also distributed cyclically across ranks to balance the triangular loop.\n- **CMake** enables the CUDA language, compiles the existing `.cpp` via nvcc with the `LANGUAGE CUDA` source property, links MPI, OpenMP and cudart, and defaults the CUDA architecture to the build machine's GPUs if not overridden.\n\n**Numerical equivalence.** The system is chaotic with a tiny softening and the result hash is exact bitwise, so I inspected the assembly GCC emits for the serial inner loop and reproduced its exact FMA contraction pattern with explicit `fma()` calls, keeping the j-summation order and disabling further contraction with `-fmad=false`. Hashes match the serial build exactly for 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 ranks and for n = 5, 1024, 4096, 8192 and 65536. The printed energy differs only in the last two of 15 significant digits because the reduction order changes.\n\n**Performance** on this 4x RTX 3090 node:\n\n| Case | Serial | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| n=8192, 10 steps | 4981 ms | | | 123 ms (8 ranks) |\n| n=65536, 5 steps | | 2400 ms | 1217 ms | 634 ms |\n\nScaling across GPUs is near linear. Edge cases (zero bodies, fewer bodies than ranks, `-h`, unknown option) behave like the original, with rank 0 doing all printing.\n\nOne note: the kernel uses IEEE double-precision divide and sqrt rather than fast approximations, because that is required for bit-exactness with the reference. Dropping that constraint would roughly double GPU throughput but change the hash."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1270,"cache_read_input_tokens":40857,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1270},"output_tokens":788,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc2352e8-6bf1-4f28-a80a-ebd683e1227b","uuid":"ce14e42f-f98a-486b-82b5-630d7595964b","timestamp":"2026-10-17T10:47:14.331Z","request_id":"req_011Cg7gASogr42YyB6CKpkox"}
